title: Desktop bootstrap launch is best-effort, detached, and must not fail the run
answers: Why doesn't a desktop bootstrap failure fail the cloud task run?
Why is the desktop bootstrap launched with setsid?
body:
`_prepare_posthog_desktop_cloud_task` (products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/provision_sandbox.py) must return quickly and never raise.
- Launch failures (exception or non-zero exit) are logged with `logger.warning("desktop_bootstrap_launch_failed")`, not raised; the agent can run the bootstrap itself.
- Exit 3 from the launch script means the branch lacks the wait script; the build is skipped so an unrebased branch never runs an install the agent cannot wait on.
- The build uses `setsid` because the sandbox runtime reaps exec children on return.
- The build's deadline is `timeout -k 30` inside the script, not an activity timeout.
- A relaunch (retried clone/checkout activity) kills the running launcher and build process group (`timeout` leads its own group, so a second kill on `-build.pid` is needed) before `rm -rf` of the state dir, since the retry recloned the tree.
- Clone/checkout activities in both process_task/workflow.py and execute_sandbox/workflow.py now use a plain 5-minute `start_to_close_timeout`; the former 20-minute desktop budget was removed, so don't reintroduce blocking bootstrap work there.
applies: Sandbox provisioning activities in tasks temporal workflows
